clue.text: Good looking husband — with a lot more, too!

parts.note: the idiom 'and some' means and plenty more besides, as in 'he paid that and some'

explanation.surface: A spouse is praised as attractive, with a jokey suggestion that he is far more than merely that.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'and some' is a colloquial intensifier meaning 'and a good deal more', which is why the whole phrase after the dash supplies those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An attractive man is described with this adjective, a straightforward synonym for good-looking.

clue.text: Hard to take in intensity of feeling

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
to take in food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to absorb a wave of strong emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: In the heat of the moment, passion runs high: the word names emotional fervour as well as warmth.

clue.text: Inquisitive father's boy slipped up on study, finally

indicators.note: in a down entry, something that slips up is read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a father's boy is his son

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word study

explanation.surface: A curious child makes a mistake while reading a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipped up' turns SON upwards into NOS; 'on' is only a link placing it above the Y in a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone prying into others' affairs is called this, a common informal synonym for curious.

clue.text: Dali, perhaps, reinterpreted rural sites

indicators.note: to reinterpret something is to recast it in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter has given his own take on scenes of the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reinterpreted' rearranges the letters of RURAL SITES.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dali was the most famous painter of the movement founded by Breton, so he is an example of the type; 'perhaps' flags that.

clue.text: My wand nearly is involved in occult rites

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a wand is a stick, as a magician's or conductor's is

explanation.surface: A conjurer's wand almost features in a secret magical ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the final K from STICK to leave STIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things concerned with spiritual mysteries and esoteric ritual, matching an occult practice.

clue.text: Antiphonal effect covered by the choir

indicators.note: the answer is concealed, covered over by the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A call-and-response musical effect is performed by the church choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered by' signals the letters hidden across thE CHOir.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiphonal singing has one group answering another, a sound repeated back like a reverberation.

clue.text: Applaud tango music that's rubbish

parts.note: to applaud is to clap
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet
rap is a genre of music

explanation.surface: A critic claps at dance music while insisting it is worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means pretentious nonsense or empty talk, a synonym for drivel.

clue.text: Fail to notice finished appearance

parts.note: something finished is over
a look is an appearance, as in 'the look of the place'

explanation.surface: Someone misses spotting the final look of a piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss something by not seeing it is a common synonym of the verb meaning to ignore or miss.

clue.text: Difficult to understand cruel treatment imprisoning three leaders of strike

indicators.note: one piece holds another inside it, as a prison holds a prisoner

parts.note: abuse is cruel treatment

indicators.note: the leading three letters of the word strike are taken

explanation.surface: A puzzling report about harsh treatment of jailed strike organisers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three leaders of' means the opening trio of letters of strike, not the heads of three words; 'imprisoning' encloses them.
explanation.definitionFit: An obscure, recondite argument is hard to grasp; the word is a learned synonym for that.

clue.text: Come to funeral party

definitions.meaning: to come to is to regain consciousness, to rouse from sleep
a gathering after a burial, with food and drink, especially in Irish tradition

explanation.surface: An invitation to attend a gathering after a burial.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to stop sleeping, and the noun is a post-burial vigil or gathering.

clue.text: Angrily criticise after food shop is slow and cautious

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other, so the shop goes first

parts.note: a deli, short for delicatessen, is a food shop
to berate is to scold angrily

explanation.surface: A customer complains furiously that the grocer's service is sluggish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' reverses the clue's order: the shop comes first in the answer. 'slow and cautious' is the adjective, not the verb meaning to ponder.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhurried, careful movement or speech is described with this adjective, as in a measured, unrushed pace.

clue.text: Like an army unit get manlier when freshly deployed

indicators.note: troops deployed afresh are placed in a new arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Soldiers become more macho on being sent out on a new posting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freshly deployed' rearranges GET MANLIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment is a military unit, and the adjective describes anything belonging to or resembling one.

clue.text: Is mother after cleaner showing attractive personality?

indicators.note: the first pieces come after the cleaner, which leads

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a British term for a cleaner
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether Mum, following the cleaning lady, is the one with real allure.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a dated British name for a woman paid to clean homes; 'after' places the other two pieces behind her.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a compelling personal magnetism that draws others, the quality of a natural leader.

clue.text: Around university, raged at changing what students do on degree day

definitions.text: what students do on degree day

indicators.note: one piece goes around another, enclosing it
changing means the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stormed angrily around campus about changes to the commencement ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges RAGED AT, and 'Around' wraps those letters round U.
explanation.definitionFit: At a degree ceremony students formally receive their qualification, the verb for completing a course.

clue.text: Leader in Hastings, a king from a long time ago?

definitions.text: Leader in Hastings, a king from a long time ago?

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word Hastings is taken

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
something from a long time ago is old

explanation.surface: A question about the English king who commanded at the battle of 1066.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: Harold Godwinson led the English at the Battle of Hastings in 1066, nearly a thousand years ago.
explanation.definitionFit: King Harold II was the Anglo-Saxon monarch defeated and killed at Hastings in 1066.

clue.text: Really angry about one king initially overlooking Japanese emperor

indicators.note: one piece goes about, surrounding, the others

parts.note: mad means really angry
I is the Roman numeral for one
K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word overlooking

explanation.surface: A furious monarch is passed over in favour of an Asian ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I and K inside MAD, and 'initially' adds O from overlooking.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a historical title used in the West for the ruler of Japan, as in Gilbert and Sullivan's operetta.

clue.text: Notice puzzling question about time

indicators.note: the first piece goes about, surrounding, the second

parts.note: a poser is a puzzling question

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on a baffling question concerning time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' looks like a verb but is a noun here: a printed announcement on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A placard put up to advertise or announce something is a public notice.

clue.text: Again find record finished after second note?

indicators.note: the record and finished pieces come after the note, which leads

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a disc is a record
something finished is over

explanation.surface: A collector wonders whether an old album resurfaces after a further musical tone.
explanation.walkthrough: In tonic sol-fa (do, re, mi...) the second note is re; 'after' places the record and finished pieces behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: To come upon something once more after it was lost is to locate it a second time.

clue.text: Grain store is put up on empty lido

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up reads it from bottom to top, so backwards
an empty word has its inside removed, leaving just the outside letters of lido

explanation.surface: A grain store is built on top of a deserted open-air pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns IS into SI; 'empty' keeps only L and O of lido. A lido is a public outdoor swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm tower for storing grain or fodder in bulk is a common sight in rural landscapes.

clue.text: Rubber ring in polystyrene

indicators.note: the answer sits within the letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A rubber ring made of foam packaging plastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the letters hidden in polySTYREne.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber casing fitted round a wheel rim is a ring of rubber on a car or bicycle.

clue.text: Gawp mostly, to see famous artiste

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: to gawp is to stare

explanation.surface: Fans gape in order to glimpse a celebrated performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last E from STARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated actor or performer is a celebrity, the leading light of a show.

clue.text: Make several levels of street sign

parts.note: to ratify a treaty is to sign it into force

explanation.surface: A road sign is made to sit on several tiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' looks like a noun beside 'street' but works as a verb: to ratify.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange something in layers or strata, as rock or social classes are, is this verb.

clue.text: Monkey with vote marking for summit

parts.note: an ape is a primate, loosely called a monkey
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A primate casts a ballot at a high-level meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summit' tempts as a political conference to match the vote, but here it is the peak.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point or tip of something, as of a mountain or triangle, is its top or peak.

clue.text: Very unpleasant morgues upset English

indicators.note: to upset something is to knock it over and disorder it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: English people are disturbed by mortuaries, which are grisly places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges MORGUES, and E is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something horrific or ghastly, especially involving death or injury, is described this way.
